summary.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose ~44% YoY to INR1,890 crore and reported EBITDA rose ~87% to INR71.5 crore (3.8% margin), with reported PBT turning positive at INR1.9 crore.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations grew about 44% YoY to INR1,890 crore, with new vehicle volumes up about 81% reported and about 91% like-to-like. Reported EBITDA rose about 87% to INR71.5 crore, margin 3.8% vs 2.9%, helped by a one-off ~INR5 crore lease-modification gain in other income. Organic revenue grew 33% YoY, indicating the existing network contributed alongside the FY26 acquisitions (RKS Maruti, Globe CV BharatBenz, Audi/Olympus). Management said the acquired businesses are now EBITDA-positive in aggregate (~INR9.4 crore) but still loss-making below EBITDA due to depreciation and finance costs; reported PAT was INR1.4 crore vs a loss of INR8.8 crore a year ago.

segments.name: Passenger Vehicles (ex-luxury)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR836 crore (+73% YoY reported, +54% excluding luxury per call); new vehicles 10,475 units (+83%); service volumes 1,90,801 (-5%) while service income INR169 crore (+11%). Organic PV revenue +49%. PV EBITDA margin ~4% per management, with Maruti ~15.5-16% and JLR ~17-18% at segment level.

segments.name: Luxury (JLR and Audi)
segments.commentary: Reported revenue +42%; new vehicles +39%; service volumes +87%. Organic luxury revenue +21%, service volumes +9%. JLR EBITDA INR10.5 crore vs INR8.2 crore a year ago; Audi EBITDA ~nil, with margin dip attributed to Audi.

segments.name: Commercial Vehicles
segments.commentary: Revenue INR564 crore (+33% reported, +35% per call; organic +21%); new vehicles 3,495 units (+41%); service volumes 52,647 (+15%), service income INR107 crore (+47%). Sequentially volumes moderated vs Q4. Management cites CV EBITDA ~3.6-3.75%.

segments.name: EV (Ather two-wheelers and e-VITARA)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR55 crore (+122% YoY; reported EV revenue +113%); new vehicles 3,330 units (+153%); service volumes 13,232 (+60%), service income ~INR3 crore. EBITDA ~INR2 crore; margin ~3.4%.

guidance_outlook: Management expects acquired businesses to be PAT-positive from Q2 FY27 onwards; RKS and Olympus targeted for PAT profitability by end of Q3, with Olympus possibly one more quarter.
RKS service volumes expected on track by Q4 FY27.
PV service volume growth expected at ~6-7% from Q2 (not the 15% previously guided), with ASP continuing to rise; Maruti service volumes expected to reach double digit from Q2.
Blended EBITDA margin: management hopes to reach ~4% and says ~4.3-4.4% by year end; 5% unlikely this year unless mix changes.
FY27 revenue targeted at INR8,200-8,300 crore vs ~INR6,400 crore in FY26 (~20-25% growth).
H2 PV growth so far running ~80-90% YoY in most months, expected to moderate on high base; Q3 flagged as key with Audi launch.
Capex limited to replacement and ongoing projects; no acquisition or expansion planned; surplus cash to be used first for debt reduction.
capex_capacity: Q1 network additions: new Maruti Suzuki service centre at Koyilandy (Kerala), two Tata CV outlets at Perumbavoor and Kazhakuttam, and a JLR sales and service facility in Nagpur.
New vehicle inventory ~32 days vs ~50 days a year ago; absolute inventory up only ~14% YoY despite higher revenue; sequential build ahead of festive season and OEM launches.
Audi inventory elevated, expected to fall to ~20-25 days in August-September.
Ather inventory ~5 days, JLR supply somewhat constrained.
Keralam revenue share fell below 50% for the first time (49%), state mix: Tamil Nadu 22%, Karnataka 12%, Telangana 8%, Maharashtra 5%, Punjab 4%, Andhra Pradesh 0.3%.
demand_pricing: Pre-festive inquiries up ~20% YoY over recent days, ~17-18% over the last month; bookings up ~22% YoY.
Keralam inauspicious period ends 16 August; retail expected to pick up from 17 August (Onam-Chingam).
CV demand weak in construction: tipper segment low to negative growth; SCV and cargo holding.
Maruti price increases modest (INR5,000-7,000 for most models; INR10,000-15,000 for some), with no major impact on demand or margin.
Entry-level cars recovered: Alto K10 and WagonR strong; S-Presso slowing; Arena returned to growth.
Spare parts short supply in the market, causing vehicles to stay in workshops.
Running repairs up ~8.8% in July; free service turned to growth in Q1.
Commercial ticket size ~INR16-17 lakh is pulling blended margin down.
